title: Hearing history being made with Garner, Lester, Parker and Tatum
summary: He says Garner's style was unlike anyone else's and that playing with these men boosted his confidence.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: When Erroll walked into the Casablanca that night and you heard him play, had you ever heard anybody play in a style like that?
Never, before or since. There are a lot of people that try to copy Erroll, but they don't even come close.
What did you think? What was your reaction? Besides that you were at his left and you saw how to play with him, what did you think about that sound?

I was utterly, totally thrilled. I knew... You know, when I had worked with Lester, I knew that was history, you know; I knew that was one of things. I said, "This guy is going down in history." The same with Charlie Parker, and naturally Art Tatum was already in the history books. And I felt so fortunate. "Gee, I must be doing something right; these guys like the way I play." So that had to be good for my ego, being young and... Well, it was just good for me. And I still remember these moments with pride and joy.
You said you recorded with Erroll for Ross Russell. Is that right?
